name: Cecil Hooper
life: “I still remember bringing slippers to three houses in one storm.” Saturday often includes a stop at Maré Coffee, where Cecil likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I can deliver to the whole ward in my lunch hour if somebody will lend me a bicycle.
appearance: Cecil is easy to recognize by thick, tightly coiled hair and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Usually dressed in a moss-green cardigan with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light, Cecil holds eye contact until the other person has finished when listening.
personality: Cecil finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To borrow a bike for the ward delivery round.
family: Lee Carr is Cecil’s cousin raised in the same household. Cecil offers the first invitation. Lee gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The worker who couldn't read the joke*, Lee says, “I used to avoid the break room. We are holding one lunch where people can explain what actually makes them laugh.”
connections: Rain Daniels. The courier's route makes a practical place for easy-to-find names on labels.

reactions.situation: A visitor offers shoes that are far too large
reactions.response: Cecil offers to look for a usable pair before anyone is asked to walk in loose shoes.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Cecil puts distance between the frightened person and the argument and asks nearby staff for help.

reactions.situation: When thanked for a shared success
reactions.response: Cecil points to the person who noticed the original mistake.
